brief.summary: Four consistent forecast advisories and many independent news reports agree that Cyclone Remal will make landfall on the West Bengal and Bangladesh coast near the Sundarbans around 19:00 UTC on 26 May, about 13 hours from now. The main gaps are the lack of river forecasts and a GDACS wind and alert value that was revised after the event.

reasons.text: All four advisories send the storm north into the northern Bay of Bengal, with computed landfall near 21.8N 88.93E around 18:55 UTC on 26 May, and the latest update moved the track only 10.3 km and the timing 1.1 hours earlier.

reasons.text: Earlier advisories shifted the track west by up to 65 km, from about 89.4E to 88.9E. That moves the core toward the India-Bangladesh border Sundarbans but keeps both the West Bengal and Bangladesh coasts exposed, so it changes little about who is at risk.
